VIDEOMovNat Trainer Certification

Before watching: What is the difference between “exercise” and “natural movement”? Which everyday movements can train the whole body?

Part 1 · What MovNat is

00:00–00:59
Readable transcript. The user-supplied auto-captions have been lightly cleaned for punctuation, obvious recognition errors and repeated filler; the meaning and content are preserved.

We've created the MovNat Certification course to share the knowledge of movement efficiency and to create a community of professionals who are dedicated to helping others get back to their birthright of moving naturally: moving with power, moving with grace, moving with ease, and moving with pleasure.

We're teaching them the MovNat system, which is based on movements that are natural to human beings: walking, running, jumping, balancing, climbing, lifting and carrying, throwing and catching. What the MovNat system focuses on is helping people and teaching people how to do it skillfully and in a way that is safe: sequence, timing, tension and relaxation.

Part 2 · What the course teaches

00:59–01:26
Readable transcript. The user-supplied auto-captions have been lightly cleaned for punctuation, obvious recognition errors and repeated filler; the meaning and content are preserved.

If you attend the course, you can expect to learn MovNat fundamental techniques, movement efficiency principles, coaching efficiency, programming, and a variety of movement variations and drills.

At the end of the certification, there will be an evaluation where your general understanding is assessed, your personal physical competence is assessed, and your coaching ability is also assessed.

Part 3 · What participants learn

01:26–03:00
Readable transcript. The user-supplied auto-captions have been lightly cleaned for punctuation, obvious recognition errors and repeated filler; the meaning and content are preserved.

One participant says: “I wanted to have more real options for real-life applicable training and things that really help, just from a corrective manner too. I'm looking forward to using this material at home with my clients. I think that the coaching and education has been fantastic, with a bit of humor, which is always good. It's been great. I would definitely recommend it, and I look forward to sending my trainers at some point to come through the certification at a future date.”

Another participant says that many movements people think they know how to do, such as squatting, walking or running, may actually be performed incorrectly. Even basic movements can become a workout. “It's been like an awakening for me. You think you're fit, but try to do a little bit of MovNat and you'll see.”

A further participant says: “I'm taking away from the course a renewed appreciation for basic movement. After this certification, I'm sore in places that I haven't been sore in a really long time, just from very basic movements: crawling, running, jumping, very, very elemental movements. For me, it's sort of like learning that the conditioning, the strengthening, is contained within the movement. Learning how to incorporate that into what I'm already teaching and coaching is something I'm really looking forward to.”

Part 4 · Why participants recommend it

03:00–04:04
Readable transcript. The user-supplied auto-captions have been lightly cleaned for punctuation, obvious recognition errors and repeated filler; the meaning and content are preserved.

One participant says the course felt like the best entry into the path of fitness coaching because of the principles it teaches. The coaches are described as “masterful”: being a great teacher is one thing, but being able to teach people how to teach is another.

The course is recommended to anyone interested in improving people's lives by getting them to move more and better. One participant argues that people cannot be healthy or free of suffering unless they move in the right way and move regularly. He describes MovNat as a system with principles that apply universally to humans and to how they should move.

A: Hi, I’m calling about the MovNat training course in November. B: OK, great. Are you interested in coming on the course? A: Yes, I am, but I’ve just got a few questions I’d like to ask. B: Right. Fire away. A: Well, the first question is, do you need to have a good level of fitness? It’s just that I’m quite unfit at the moment. Does that matter? I mean, do I need to go to the gym before I begin the course? B: No, no. The course is for anybody. It doesn’t matter how fit you are. When you arrive, the instructor will check your fitness level and will then divide you into two groups, beginner and intermediate. A: Right. Sounds good. I was also wondering about the weather. The course is outdoors, isn’t it? It’s in a park. What will happen if it rains or snows? Will you cancel it or will it be indoors? B: Erm, no. With MovNat you need to practise your skills in all weather conditions. That’s part of our philosophy. The course will take place outside, whatever the weather. If it’s raining or snowing, the experience will be even more exciting! A: OK. So is it necessary to book a place, or would it be all right to just turn up? B: No, you’ll definitely need to reserve a place before you come. The courses are popular and places are limited. In fact, there are only two or three places left in November. Would you like me to book you onto the course now? A: I just need to check I can make those dates. Then I’ll call and book. B: OK. Don’t miss your place though! A: No, I won’t. I’ll get back to you as soon as I know. B: OK, sounds good. Speak to you soon, I hope.

GRAMMAR FOCUSPresent tenses in future time clauses

1 · Future meaning, present form

After when, if, as soon as, before, after, use a present tense to refer to the future.

when / if / before + PRESENT → future result
2 · Do not put will in the time clause

✓ I’ll call you when I arrive.
✗ I’ll call you when I will arrive.

3 · if vs when

Use if when the event is uncertain. Use when when you expect it to happen.

If it rains, we’ll stay inside.
When the course finishes, we’ll go home.

4 · as soon as

Use it when the second action happens immediately after the first.

As soon as I know, I’ll get back to you.

5 · before and after

Before introduces the action that happens second; after introduces the action that happens first.

I’ll stretch before I run.
After I finish, I’ll rest.

6 · Clause order

Either clause can come first. If the time/condition clause comes first, use a comma.

If it rains, we’ll train outside.
We’ll train outside if it rains.

PRACTICEControlled → productive grammar

A · Complete the conversations

Use the present simple or will + infinitive.

1A Come on. Let’s book this course before I (change) my mind about it.
1B I promise you, you (enjoy) it when you (get) there.
2A Do you think we (do) warm-up exercises before we (start)?
2B Definitely. If we (not do) any, our muscles (hurt) later.
3A I like this Paleo Diet. I think I (continue) with it after the course (finish).
3B I’m bored with it. As soon as I (leave) here, I’m going to have a big plate of chips.

B · Choose the best linker

1 I see a rare animal, I’ll take a photo.
2 The weather will slowly get colder autumn arrives.
3 We’re really tired, so we’ll sleep we arrive at the camp.
4 I’ll walk back I get lost.
5 We’ll go travelling in the Amazon we have more money.
6 a snake bites you, you’ll have to go to hospital.
7 It’ll be dark soon. We’ll have to return to camp we reach the mountain top.

C · Complete the jungle-trip advertisement

Use the correct form of the verbs in brackets.

After you get off (get off) the bus at Monkey River Village, you (travel) up the river for five to six kilometres.

As soon as the boat (reach) the jungle trail, you (walk) into the jungle to look for Howler monkeys.

Cover your ears when you (hear) them.

Before you (leave), you (have) the opportunity to swim in the river.

As soon as the group (be) dry and ready to go, we (return) to the village.

D · Rewrite the two sentences as one

Use the word in brackets. More than one word order may be possible.

1 You’re going to the countryside. You’ll feel better. (when)
2 We’ll get to the waterfall. We’ll see a bridge. (after)
3 We might not see the island. It might be cloudy. (if)
4 The sun will come out today. Will we go for a bike ride? (when)
5 The leaves change colour. Then, they fall. (before)
6 The weather gets warmer. Spring flowers will appear. (as soon as)
1 You’ll feel better when you go to the countryside.
2 After we get to the waterfall, we’ll see a bridge.
3 We might not see the island if it’s cloudy.
4 Will we go for a bike ride when the sun comes out today?
5 The leaves change colour before they fall.
6 As soon as the weather gets warmer, spring flowers will appear.

SPEAKINGUse the language actively

1. Would you prefer MovNat to a normal gym workout? Why?
Sample: I would probably enjoy MovNat because the exercises are based on basic movement and seem more applicable to real life than using machines in a gym.
2. What will you do if the weather is bad when you plan to exercise outside?
Sample: If it rains lightly, I’ll probably continue training outside. If the weather becomes dangerous, I’ll train indoors instead.
3. What will you do as soon as you finish your next workout?
Sample: As soon as I finish my next workout, I’ll drink some water and do a few minutes of easy recovery work.
4. Which natural movements do adults stop doing as they get older? Should they practise them?
Sample: Many adults stop climbing, crawling, balancing and jumping. I think basic movement is useful because it can improve coordination and make everyday movement easier.
